## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Suhanujātaka* (Ja 158) is a narrative belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection. In the edition of the commentary by V. Fausböll, it is situated as the eighth story of its vagga, opening with the canonical verse beginning *Na-y-idam visamasīlena* [Fausböll 1879].

The framing narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana, where the Buddha delivers the teaching concerning two hot-tempered, violent monks (*dve caṇḍabhikkhū*) [Fausböll 1879]. In the tale of the past (*atītavatthu*), horse dealers troubled by a vicious royal horse named Mahāsoṇa consult the Bodhisatta, who serves as a wise minister (*paṇḍitāmacco*) to the king [Fausböll 1879]. The Bodhisatta instructs them to bring another notoriously fierce horse named Suhanu from their home city to confront it [Fausböll 1879]. In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the two unruly horses were the two hot-tempered monks, the king was Ānanda, and the wise minister was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1879].
